hero: Hydro jetting around Tallmadge Circle can clear grease, scale and roots from drain lines serving some of the city's oldest properties. The Circle was laid out in 1807, so buildings nearby have often been altered and repaired many times. A camera inspection first shows what the line is made of and whether it can take high-pressure cleaning.
bodyH2: Hydro Jetting for Properties Around the Circle
bodyPs: The [[City of Tallmadge|https://www.tallmadgeoh.gov/210/Our-History]] says the community was founded in 1807 by the Reverend David Bacon, who laid out the Circle on a New England town plan with eight roads running out from a central core. The [[Summit County Historical Society|https://www.summithistory.org/Tallmadge]] adds that the Circle, with its First Congregational Church and Old Town Hall, was placed on the National Register of Historic Places in 1971.

Early development followed those roads outward from the center, so homes closest to the Circle are among the oldest in the city. The [[Beacon Journal|https://www.beaconjournal.com/story/news/local/2013/03/24/local-history-tallmadge-circle-is/10606259007/]] reports that Bacon planned the roads 66 feet wide at 45-degree angles from a 7½-acre central square. A house or shop near the center may have gone through additions, conversions and pipe replacements. Each change is a place where buildup can start.
Hydro jetting can clear a sound line of grease, scale and roots. It is not a fix for a broken pipe, which needs a repair plan.
